Highly transparent volumes require full ray traversal, while opaque volumes benefit significantly from early termination [S17, unofficial].

The evidence explicitly describes a volume rendering algorithm that uses front-to-back ray traversal. It states that rays are terminated early when accumulated opacity exceeds a threshold (0.98). The notes further clarify that this early termination 'significantly reduces computation for opaque areas' (supporting the claim that opaque volumes benefit) and that the threshold 'may cause slight underestimation of final color for highly transparent regions' (implying that for highly transparent volumes, the full traversal is necessary or that early termination is less effective/accurate, thus requiring full traversal for accuracy). Therefore, the claim that highly transparent volumes require full ray traversal (to avoid underestimation) while opaque volumes benefit from early termination is supported by the provided text.
